blind.why: Long-lane haze at ~18 m (N_far) vs CS2 t4_024. The ref smoke spreads low and wide, takes on the blue-grey of the shaded scene, has ragged edges that dissolve, and a tracer visibly tears it. Ours is a bright white cotton block with a scalloped outline, flat light, and a hard vertical cut where it meets the Long wall. It reads clearly but looks pasted into the scene.

L_haze_2 vs t4_009. The ref smoke flows around the crates, takes the warm local colour, has a lit side and a shaded side, and its edges thin out. Ours is a uniform grey-white cumulus of same-size lobes with almost no self-shadowing.

Aim arc (utility-lab preview_arc) vs CS2 t4_008. Ours is a thin, faint cyan thread that foreshortens straight down the corridor, and the landing ring is barely visible. The ref line is thick, glows, and shows every bounce.

biggest_gap: Haze still looks like a cotton-wool impostor, not volumetric smoke. Repro: test=1&seed=1, debug.spawn('haze',{x:38,y:.07,z:6}), wait 6 s. Viewed from (38,1.62,24) (N_far) it is a near-white cumulus of equal round lobes with a crisp scalloped silhouette, a hard vertical edge against the Long wall (no depth-soft fade), and almost flat lighting (no lit side vs shade side). Up close after a shot (N_spray, from z=16) the large circular puff discs show their rims, and a separate round ball floats off the right side. The ground skirt wisps are not visible at 18 m. CS2 (t4_009/t4_024) has a broad low silhouette, edges that break into wisps, strong directional shading, scene-tinted ambient light (grey-blue in shade), and soft contact with walls. Fixes: blend puffs against scene depth (soft particles), add a much stronger sun/shade gradient across the cloud, mix in scene ambient colour, vary lobe scale, and cull or merge stray outlier puffs.
other_gaps: The aim preview misreports where a Haze lands. trajectory() stops after 3 bounces, but a Haze keeps rolling until it rests (up to 3 s). Repro: test=1&seed=1, place(0,0,36,0,0.22), strong haze. The preview/landing ring ends at z=11.2 in front of Mid Doors, but the smoke pops at z=3.9 in Hub, 7.4 m further and through the doorway. Either simulate to rest for haze or add more rolling friction.

Attackers almost never smoke. Over 8 bot-lab rounds (seeds 3 and 7, 9000 credits), 9 of 10 Hazes were thrown by TIDE and EMBER threw 1. EMBER's utility was mostly Strobes (11). CS2 executes smoke the CT crosses (A-site angles from Long/Catwalk).

Bot strobe quality is low. 19 bot strobes produced only 5 enemy blinds at >=0.5 (26%). The same lineup was repeated with no effect: Ryo strobed (40,-13) in R2 and R4, blinding no enemy and blinding himself 0.27/0.30. Team-flash is now fixed: 0 ally blinds >=0.5.

The aim arc is too thin and faint in both the lab and the map. On the real map (m_preview) only a short cyan stub near the crosshair is visible, and the ring is hidden behind cover. It needs a thicker line, a visible-through-geometry occluded segment, and bounce markers.

The Pulse dome renders through walls. In P_c the 7 m hex dome cuts into the Long buildings on both sides, while the damage is correctly wall-blocked. Clip or fade the dome where it intersects the map.
Strobe 'full white' is at 0.975 opacity. At pop+0.05 s the HUD and the scene outlines still show faintly. CS2's peak is solid white.
bugs: Haze preview landing point does not match the pop point (see other_gaps[0]); the player is misled by about 7 m on flat ground.
strengths: Team-flash is fixed: 0 ally/self blinds >=0.5 over 43 bot throws in 8 rounds, and throw volume is up (19 and 24 per 4 rounds).
The Haze confines well to the Long lane and fills it wall to wall. Inside it is properly opaque murk.
The Strobe whiteout, quadratic fade and blurred afterimage read well.
Pulse is distinct and readable: hex dome, ground ring and dust, no whiteout.
utility_test 31/31 pass, no console errors, LOS punch-through matches the screen.
